verses.pali: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahāpathaviyā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhipeyya.
verses.english: “Mendicants, suppose a person was to place seven clay balls the size of jujube seeds on the great earth.

verses.pali: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ—yā vā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā, ayaṁ vā mahāpathavī”ti?
verses.english: Which is more: the seven clay balls the size of jujube seeds, or the great earth?”

verses.pali: “Etadeva, bhante, bahutaraṁ, yadidaṁ—mahāpathavī; appamattikā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā.
verses.english: “Sir, the great earth is certainly more. The seven clay balls the size of jujube seeds are tiny.

verses.pali: Saṅkhampi na upenti, upanidhampi na upenti, kalabhāgampi na upenti mahāpathaviṁ upanidhāya satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā”ti.
verses.english: Compared to the great earth, they don’t count, there’s no comparison, they’re not worth a fraction.”
“In the same way, for a noble disciple …
That’s why you should practice meditation …”
